name: the side menu opened from the home screen

regions_read.verdict_on_region: the app's own name at the head of the drawer — names the app, not a place in it
contains_selected_view: false and no item is visibly highlighted — lists where you could go, not where you are

identifier_found: none; the drawer head is the app's name "Claude" and no drawer item is highlighted
accessibility_text: "Claude" is the content_description of the head button; nothing names a current section
initial_rationale: the only header text is the app's name and the navigation list has no active item, so neither locates the user

test_cases.action: tap the three-line menu glyph and look at the drawer for a highlighted item
test_cases.expected_result: either one drawer item is visibly highlighted, or none is
test_cases.confirms_if: no item is highlighted and the head shows only "Claude"
test_cases.overturns_if: an item is highlighted, locating the user
test_cases.observed_result: drawer opened: head "Claude"; Chats, Projects, Code, Artifacts all drawn alike with no fill; "Recents" with two "Untitled" rows below (not in the capture)

deciding_evidence: live: opening the drawer from the home screen shows "Claude" at the head and no highlighted item among Chats, Projects, Code, Artifacts (a Recents list now follows them). The same drawer opened from Chats/Projects/Code does highlight the current item (s9, s44), so the absence here is specific to arriving from the home screen, which belongs to no listed section.
recommendation: when the drawer is opened from the home screen, show which place the user came from — e.g. a highlighted "New chat" entry — rather than the bare app name
